label: Sixth-edition aphorisms
title: Aphorism § 140
text:
§ 140



 If the person cannot write, the physician must be informed by him
          every day of what has occurred to him, and how it took place. What is noted down as
          authentic information on this point, however, must be chiefly the voluntary narration of
          the person who makes the experiment, nothing conjectural and as little as possible derived
          from answers to leading questions should be admitted; everything must be ascertained with
          the same caution as I have counselled above (§§ 84-99) for the investigation of the
          phenomena and for tracing the picture of natural diseases.
